newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 3/8 amid bid lists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 3/8 amid bid lists.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were up 3/8 of a point as plentiful customer lists drew strong interest from bidders, traders said.
"It's been a good day today," one trader said, adding that while "the bid wanted wires have not been light," bidding was aggressive and broad-based.

"I don't think there is any concession in our market right now," he said. "With the (Federal Reserve) on hold for now and the fact that the calendar is so light..you kind of have to take your shots right now on the secondary side, you know, on the bid wanteds."
While he hadn't added them up, the trader said he saw 10 to 11 lists in circulation from funds and other accounts.

"It's kind of interesting, they are all selling kind of the same area, '05 to '09 and then '10 to '16," the trader said. "We had one little list of 25-(year) and 30-year paper but in terms of par value it paled in comparison to this other stuff."
A second trader reported seeing about 22 bid lists out.
"I haven't added up the par amount, but (there was) a lot of selling today," he said.
Traders attributed municipals' strength to Federal Reserve policy makers' decision to stand pat on interest rates.

"Definitely the market has a better tone since the Fed didn't act," one trader said. He added, however, "I thought that we had room to improve even if they did raise 25 basis point because I think we were a little overdone."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 19/32 at 07-20/32 to yield 6.94 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 11/32 at 113-31/32. The December T-bond contract was up 19/32 at 109-7/32. The MOB spread was 152 ticks.
